next_action.description: Gate E - MiniMax H3. 1.4 is the H3 release, so the version bump is the LAST step, not the next one (the previous close-out named the bump and was wrong: the umbrella brief still had MPI-449 on its not-in-1.4 list from when H3 was open research). Start by reading MPI-450's brief section 'Gate E'. The chain is MPI-449 -> MPI-451 -> MPI-452 and cannot be reordered. MPI-449 only needs closing out - H3 is already MEASURED running on the 4060 Ti 16 GB - but it is a PEER's active card (commits f739e076, d5b858ef), so coordinate before touching it. The real work is MPI-451, the licence gate: our H3 authorization is conditioned on binding each user to terms at least as protective as the Use Restrictions and AUP, so there is no legal route to ship the model without it, and it is a genuine feature (licence descriptor on the ModelDef, terms UI, per-model acceptance that survives a restart, the licensor's own authorization route for the territory restriction). MPI-452 then wires the model and carries the engine bump off the 0.29.2 pin to 0.30.x - run the custom-node pairing check FIRST per .claude/rules/comfy_engine.md.

key_decisions: SCOPE, user 2026-08-05: 1.4 ships WITH MiniMax H3. MPI-449 was removed from the umbrella's 'explicitly NOT in 1.4' list - that exclusion predates the measurement showing H3 runs locally. The version bump is therefore gated behind MPI-449 -> MPI-451 -> MPI-452, and the ENGINE BUMP to 0.30.x now lands inside 1.4.
MPI-404: the models root stays ENGINE-OWNED (user, 2026-08-05). The hero must not assert a count it cannot compute. An app-level models root is a product card of its own if ever wanted.

MPI-410 root, MEASURED not guessed: mainWindow's ready-to-show fires on Chromium's network error page, so the splash was closed 1.1s BEFORE Express bound. did-finish-load fires for the error page too and getURL() keeps the target URL - only did-navigate separates them. The splash was never starved (81ms to load), so the brief's candidate 2 is dead.

MPI-412 root: indeterminate was a per-TICK flag, so the display mode flipped on whichever dep ticked last. routes/install/computeProgress.js already held the correct job-level rule, was tested by MPI-276, and was required by NOTHING - the live path kept a divergent copy. Only isNodeTickPending is wired in so far; adopting computeProgress wholesale would change verify/phase semantics for the Model Library and needs its own card.

MPI-416 split by Gate C: the symlink half shipped, the Xcode CLT half is deferred behind a known-issue line. Do NOT start the tarball-instead-of-clone fix from the card text - CLT also supplies clang, so killing git may only move the dialog later. Verify that first.

MPI-433 stays date-gated (maturity blocked). The audit found THREE more single-route deps than that card knew about - the MPI-420 preview decoders - and they are permanently noMirror by nature, not by licence timing. Do not fold them into MPI-433's rollback.
Gate B runs AFTER the bump on purpose: MPI-249 tests the ARTIFACT, and verifying a dev checkout does not verify a build.
